title: Plus One
pattern: Add from the right, carry while the digit is 9
statement: A large integer is given as an array of its `digits`, most significant digit first. Add one to the integer and return the resulting array of digits.

example.why: 199 + 1 = 200: both 9s roll over to 0 and the carry finally lands on the 1.

idea: Adding one affects the **last** digit first, exactly as on paper.
If that digit is less than 9, increase it and stop — nothing else changes. If it is 9, it becomes 0 and the `+1` **carries** to the digit on its left.
If the carry runs past the first digit (the number was all 9s), the result needs one more digit: a leading 1.

complexity.timeWhy: At most one pass over the digits; usually it stops at the last digit.
complexity.spaceWhy: In place (a new list is built only when every digit was 9).

steps.text: Our example: **`digits = [1,9,9]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
The digit at index 2 is 9: 9 + 1 = 10. Write **0** here and **carry** the 1 to the digit on the left.
The digit at index 1 is 9: 9 + 1 = 10. Write **0** here and **carry** the 1 to the digit on the left.
The digit at index 0 is 1, less than 9: add 1 → **2**. No carry is produced, so we are finished.
Done — the answer is **`[2,0,0]`**. 199 + 1 = 200: both 9s roll over to 0 and the carry finally lands on the 1.
